static_traits.name: Li Bo
static_traits.social_status: Has a group of supportive friends, but interpersonal relationships are tense due to catastrophizing tendencies; has not yet discussed cognitive patterns with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological issues; never received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good cooperativeness; rather negative tone; able to self-reflect but often using absolutist expressions, easily focusing on negatives and ignoring positives

basic_info.main_problem: Tending to catastrophize small setbacks and completely negate the whole experience (e.g. a shell picked up at the beach cracking in the car leads to seeing the entire trip as utterly meaningless); this pattern started about a year ago and has worsened recently, often appearing when things do not go as planned, causing positives to be ignored and only negatives focused on.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizing the catastrophizing tendency is affecting the overall outlook on life and causing unnecessary suffering, thus seeking counseling; hoping to remind oneself that 'one small thing will not ruin everything'.
growth_experiences: About a year ago encountered a series of small setbacks in personal life (e.g. friends canceling plans, losing beloved small items); since then gradually formed and reinforced catastrophizing and black-and-white cognitive patterns around small things: once imperfection appears, the whole experience is completely negated. This pattern makes them increasingly ignore positives and focus only on negatives, further affecting sleep and self-care, work and interpersonal relationships.

core_beliefs: One negative event ruins the whole experience

special_situations.event: A shell picked up at the beach cracking in the car
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a flaw appears, it means this day is no longer perfect and the whole trip loses meaning
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing attention on negative details, negating or ignoring other positive experiences to maintain the 'perfect' standard
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The whole trip is utterly meaningless

special_situations.event: Friends canceling plans at the last minute
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the plan is disrupted, it means life is going downhill and I have lost control
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Preemptively negating follow-up plans, magnifying negative impact to gain 'mental preparation'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Everything is collapsing; this week is ruined

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot keep things intact and under control, it means I am incompetent/a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Intensifying self-blame and negating the day's other gains, reducing attention to positive facts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I always mess things up, cannot keep anything

special_situations.event: Small deviations at work or classes not going as planned
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the class is not perfect, it means I am incompetent and unworthy of affirmation
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses only on negative feedback or small mistakes, actively ignores the positive parts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This class was terrible; I am not a good coach

core_conflict.wish: Longs to maintain perfection and control, thereby gaining a stable sense of worth and pleasurable experience
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that any imperfection means total failure and being negated, life out of control
defense_goal: Avoiding the anxiety of facing imperfection through wholesale negation and absolutist evaluation
Maintains a focus on negative details to uphold the psychological defense line of a 'perfect standard'

object_relations.self_representation: A fragile self, easily knocked down by small setbacks, needs perfection to maintain a sense of worth
object_relations.object_representation: Others may not understand or may judge oneself; the world/situations easily 'ruin' perfect plans

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When small setbacks occur or things do not go as planned (e.g. items damaged, plans canceled), or when others invite attention to positives/integrating good and bad
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding imperfection as total failure and loss of control (transference: projecting the inner rule of 'perfect = safe' onto situations)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using absolutist expressions (e.g. 'everything is ruined'), denying or belittling positive details, tone depressed, insisting on the 'either perfect or utterly meaningless' stance.

manifestations: When small flaws appear (e.g. a shell cracking), defining the whole experience as 'utterly meaningless'
Using 'a perfect day' as the anchor of meaning, making the sense of meaning highly vulnerable to imperfection

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Evaluates experiences by the rigid rule 'should have a perfect day'
Constrains oneself with the inner standard 'one small thing ruins everything'

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Knowingly having supportive friends yet not discussing one's own troubles, keeping stress and negative rumination to oneself
When distressed, reduces outward expression and support-seeking and instead turns to self-depletion (sleep and self-care are impaired)

positive_force: Has a supportive network of friends
Having proactively tried mindfulness interventions to challenge thinking
Has self-awareness, can describe clearly and is willing to seek help
Having stable professional skills and work foundation (yoga instructor)
negative_force: Significant cognitive tendencies toward catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking
Mental filtering and negating positives, difficulty seeing positive facts
Worrying about being judged and thus not expressing troubles to supporters
Perfectionist conditions of worth leading to poor tolerance of uncertainty
Negative rumination impairs sleep and self-care

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing and black-and-white cognitive reactions after small setbacks (accompanied by low mood)
antecedent: When things do not go as planned
Small defects or damage appearing (e.g. a cracked shell)
Having plans cancelled by friends or losing a beloved item
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized perfectionist rules and the core belief of 'imperfection = failure'
target_behavior.function: Escaping the anxiety and shame brought by imperfection and uncertainty through wholesale negation of experience
target_behavior.consequence: Ignoring the positive side, work and interpersonal relations are impaired, sleep and self-care are disturbed, overall suffering worsens

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids seeking support from friends or discussing cognitive troubles
antecedent: After negative emotions or catastrophizing thoughts arise
When worrying about being seen as exaggerating or not being understood
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being judged and negated, defensively avoiding to preserve a vulnerable self-image
target_behavior.function: Escapes potential negative evaluation to maintain a sense of psychological safety
target_behavior.consequence: Support system not yet utilized, interpersonal relationships further strained, accumulating negative emotions and cognitive rumination
